# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 4 LUTs, 5 FFs, WNS 0.731 ns, and WHS 0.173 ns. The editable seed is only a wrapper around a frozen debouncer, so hierarchy changes alone cannot improve the flattened design. With `minimize_luts`, this iteration must pass every gate and use fewer than 4 LUTs to improve the incumbent; no prior trial outcomes are available.

## Hypothesis
Inlining the debouncer into the top and replacing its binary count progression with a three-bit LFSR sequence may reduce LUT use by simplifying the counter update logic, while keeping the same five state bits and debounce behavior.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the child instance with equivalent sequential logic inside `debouncer_top`, retaining the `clean_reg` and `candidate` state and the synchronous active-high reset. Replace the binary count with a three-bit state that seeds to `001`, advances through `011, 111, 110, 101, 010, 100`, and recognizes `100` as the terminal state; reset and input mismatch must restart the sequence so `clean` updates on the eighth consecutive sample. Keep `// @latency 0` and preserve all ports, registered output behavior, and observable cycles; the LFSR is only a candidate optimization, so retain it only if simulation, all metric-integrity checks, setup and hold, and the required LUT objective comparison pass.
